run.title: Acme Books Guardrails
run.heading: Acme Books
run.subject: Guardrails from PR #57
run.outcome: Turn five mistakes the review of PR #57 caught by hand into checks that fail before the next review.
run.prs: Each candidate you build becomes its own PR from `main`, labelled `guardrail`. The status enum stacks on a prep PR that fixes its 26 string sites.
run.method: Read the 14 review threads, 3 review bodies and the diff of PR #57, then the `main` branch: Pint, Rector, PHPStan with its custom rules, the Pest arch suite, the pre-commit hook and CI. Measured each candidate's violations, exceptions and run time on `main`.

why.text: A hand-built total skips the discount and VAT, so an invoice comes out low and a refund pays back too much. Three reviews caught it in three files, and summing the lines is the first thing a session writes when it needs a total. Recommended: one PHPStan rule holds it, with one exception.

quotes.text: This sums `price * quantity` over the lines by hand. `Order::total()` already does that and applies the discount and VAT, so this invoice comes out low for every discounted order.
Same hand-built total as in `RefundController`: it skips the discount, so a refund pays back more than the customer paid.
`InvoicePdf::render()` recomputes the total from `$order->lines`. Use the model's `total()` so the PDF and the checkout agree.

mistake.note: `Order::total()` applies discounts and VAT, and returns cents.

guardrail.message:
Order totals come from Order::total(), which applies discounts and VAT.
Replace this sum over $order->lines with $order->total().

tradeoff.forbids: Any sum over `$order->lines`, even one that wants the subtotal before discounts. The way past it is `Order::subtotal()`, or a `@phpstan-ignore` with the reason on the line.
tradeoff.breaks: `Order::total()` is renamed or the lines relation moves: the rule names both, so its test fails and names the rename.

cost.falsePositives: None: `Order::total()` is the one sum the rule allows
cost.newTools: None. PHPStan runs in `composer test` and CI.
cost.overlap: #61 edits `InvoicePdf.php`. Merge this one after it.

changes.title: Store order status as the `OrderStatus` enum

why.text: A misspelled status is stored as it is, so the order drops out of every status filter and the fulfilment queue with no error. `main` passes `status` as a string in 26 places, so a session copies the form it sees. A close call: the cast needs a prep PR that touches 11 files before the check can land.

quotes.text: `'shiped'` is a typo, and nothing catches it: the column takes any string, so the order drops out of every status filter.
Can we stop passing status as a string? This is the third typo this quarter.

mistake.note: The cast refuses, on write, any string that names no status.

guardrail.message: ValueError: "shiped" is not a valid backing value for enum App\Enums\OrderStatus

tradeoff.forbids: A status the enum lacks: adding one is a migration of the enum and the column check, so an experimental status needs the PR first.
tradeoff.breaks: A row written outside Eloquent (`DB::table()`, a seeder) skips the cast and stores any string again.

cost.violations: 26 string literals in 11 files. A prep PR fixes them by hand, and this PR stacks on it
cost.falsePositives: None: the cast runs on write, so a string that names a status still passes
cost.runTime: None. The cast runs on write.
cost.overlap: #63 (draft, updated 2026-10-14) adds a `refunded` status. Merge it first, or add the case here.

changes.alternative: A PHPStan rule that flags string literals passed to `status` needs no prep PR, and leaves the column free to take any string.

why.text: A `now()` call hides from a search for the clock, so a change to how the code reads time misses it, and one thing has two names. `now()` is Laravel's own helper, so every fresh session reaches for it. Recommended: Rector rewrites it on commit, so the check costs nothing to obey.

quotes.text: Nit: the rest of the codebase writes `Date::now()`, so a search for the clock misses this one.

tradeoff.forbids: Nothing: Rector rewrites `now()` to `Date::now()` and the session never sees a failure.
tradeoff.breaks: A file Rector does not read: `rector.php` lists `app` and `tests`, so a `now()` in `database/` stays.

cost.violations: 41, all rewritten by Rector in this PR
cost.falsePositives: None: every `now()` on `main` means the clock
cost.newTools: None. Rector runs in the pre-commit hook.

changes.title: Restore a deleted user before you create one for the same email

why.text: A second user row for an email a deleted account holds splits the customer's invoices across two rows, and nothing errors. One flow created the duplicate, and nothing near `User::create()` shows the deleted rows. A close call: the rule lives far from the change site, so a line is the only rung that reaches it.

quotes.text: This creates a second user for an email that belongs to a deleted account. The unique index skips deleted rows, so the old invoices stay on the old row.

mistake.note: No check can tell a fresh email from one a deleted account holds. The unique index lives in a migration, far from the code that creates users.

write: - A deleted user keeps their row, and the unique email index skips deleted rows. Before you create a user for an email, look for a deleted one with `User::withTrashed()` and restore it.

cost.violations: 1 in `InviteUser`, which the source PR fixes
cost.tokens: About 50, only in sessions that read `app/Users`
cost.loadsWhen: A session touches a file under `app/Users/`
cost.alreadyStated: No. The unique index lives in a migration, and no CLAUDE.md names it

changes.title: Send payments GraphQL only through `PaymentsClient`

why.text: A raw payments call goes out without the auth header, the idempotency key and the retries, so a retry after a timeout can refund twice. One job skipped the client in 14 months, and `PaymentsClient` sits in the same namespace as every caller. Low value: the test guards a form nobody else writes.

quotes.text: `RefundOrder` posts a raw GraphQL query with `Http::post()`. `PaymentsClient` adds the auth header, the idempotency key and retries, and this call has none of them.

guardrail.message:
app/Jobs/RefundOrder.php sends a payments GraphQL request outside PaymentsClient.
Add a method to App\Payments\PaymentsClient and call it, so the request gets auth, an idempotency key and retries.

tradeoff.forbids: Any `Http` call to the payments host from `App\Jobs`, including a one-off diagnostic. The way past it is a method on `PaymentsClient`.
tradeoff.breaks: The payments host moves to a new domain: the test matches the URL by hand, so it scans for nothing until the pattern is updated.

changes.alternative: A two-line arch test that keeps `Http` out of `App\Jobs` covers the same paths, and also blocks the jobs that call other APIs.

notNow.title: Format money only through `Money::format()`
notNow.why: 38 views call `number_format()` by hand, and fixing them needs the invoice views refactored first. That prep PR is bigger than this round.

notNow.why: The check needs ast-grep, a new tool, for one finding. Horizon's default queue already runs the jobs that miss it.
